chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza from Dawud al-Raqqi from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for a man from his wife while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'That which is below the private part.'
ai.seo_question: What is the permissible area of intercourse for a man with his wife during her menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of sexual intimacy during menstruation, specifying that intercourse below the vulva is allowed while excluding the main vaginal canal. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is derived from the general permissibility of 'what is below the khithul' (the front private part) as indicated in the Quran, distinguishing it from the specific prohibition of vaginal intercourse. The narration highlights the practical application of Quranic verses by the Imams, providing a clear legal boundary for marital relations during the state of hayd.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, drom Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Dawood Al Raqqy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is Permissible for the man, from his woman, and she is menstruating?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever is besides the front private part’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Dawud al-Riqqiy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about what is permissible for a man to enjoy with his wife during her experiencing Hayd (menses). He (the Imam) said, ‘Everything except her vulva.’”
